2.0.1

Latest release12 November 2026
  • GateFox checks for app updates when opened or activated and every five minutes while active. Available updates appear above every page and in the sidebar, with an install action and a clear quit-to-finish action after staging. Failed checks show a retry action. The existing signed updater preserves running chats.

GitHub release ↗Download for Mac

1.9.8

12 November 2026
  • An unused phone connection no longer blocks updates. The native relay kept each remote stream's engine running until the stream closed, and while its cloud connection failed with 409 Conflict the SDK's idle sweep never closed it, so one stream on macbook-server held an old release for more than eight hours and left the rollout at process_version_pending. The relay now ends a session after 10 minutes with no traffic, no running turn and no request or approval waiting (idle_released). The phone reconnects on its next use.

GitHub release ↗Download for Mac

1.9.7

12 November 2026
  • The tailnet listener now works with the App Store build of Tailscale. That build is sandboxed and could not write the certificate to the gateway's state directory ("operation not permitted"), so the listener stayed closed. The gateway now reads the certificate and key from tailscale cert output, checks that they match, and keeps them in memory only. The copy that 1.9.6 wrote is removed.

GitHub release ↗Download for Mac

1.9.6

12 November 2026
  • The tailnet listener serves HTTPS. Claude Desktop accepts a plain http:// gateway only on loopback, and its configuration window drops any other http:// URL when it saves, so the 1.9.3 endpoint could not be used. The gateway now serves the tailnet with this Mac's own Tailscale certificate (Let's Encrypt, from tailscale cert), fetches and renews it itself, and stays closed on the tailnet without one. gateway claude-desktop configure --direct --tailnet writes the https://NAME.ts.net:PORT endpoint. The tailnet must allow HTTPS certificates. The Mac app's Tailscale binary runs as its command line from the background service (TAILSCALE_BE_CLI=1); without it, it tried to open its GUI and the certificate was never fetched. 1.9.5 was not published.

GitHub release ↗Download for Mac

1.9.4

12 November 2026
  • The phone reaches a Mac again after ChatGPT 26.1106.51428, and that Mac shares its native chats again. The update ships the Codex 0.167.0-alpha.4.1 app engine, which the remote relay refused ("requires the matching Codex CLI build") and paused as failing, while the shared host reported native sharing unavailable. Its remote-control transport and processor, state migrations and auth.json format are byte-identical to the admitted 0.167.0-alpha.3.2. The rebuilt relay passed its 47 tests, the upstream remote_control suite (165) and the relay end-to-end check against the signed engine, and the engine passed every stdio and Unix shared-native phase with and without an explicit host engine path.

GitHub release ↗Download for Mac

1.9.3

11 November 2026
  • Claude Desktop Code sessions can run on another machine over SSH while using this Mac's gateway. Claude Desktop sends such a session's inference from the remote host and refuses a loopback endpoint for it, so the gateway can now also listen on this Mac's own Tailscale addresses when the configuration sets "tailnetListener": true. Only tailnet peers are accepted, and every request still needs the client token. gateway claude-desktop configure --direct --tailnet --ssh-host HOST points the profile at that address and writes the sshHostAllowlist that makes the app offer SSH environments. The listener is off by default and follows a live configuration edit without a restart.

GitHub release ↗Download for Mac

1.9.2

11 November 2026
  • The gateway can serve Claude Desktop itself. gateway claude-desktop configure --direct points the app's profile at the gateway's own port and lists one row per catalog model, including GPT accounts, local models and API models. The separate adapter process and the private inference gateway are no longer needed for a new setup; both stay supported. The gateway resolves the same Claude-safe model IDs the adapter used, clamps an effort the route does not offer, and answers GET /v1/models in Anthropic's shape for a client that sends anthropic-version or x-api-key. Other clients keep the alias list.
  • Claude Desktop configuration can opt into native behavesAs model metadata with --native-model-metadata. Secondary reasoning models keep stable opaque IDs, while older saved-chat routes remain accepted and explicit effort caps survive migration. The existing mapping remains the default.

GitHub release ↗Download for Mac

1.9.1

11 November 2026
  • Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.1 now advertise a 1M context window instead of 200K. Fable 5.2 runs through the Claude CLI's [1m] variant, because CLI 2.1.299 does not yet recognize the model and runs its plain ID at 200K. Its gateway alias keeps the plain ID, so saved chats keep working. Codex previously limited Fable 5.2 chats to about 180K, so a chat switched to it after compaction could fail with "ran out of room in the model's context window". Sonnet 4.6 and Haiku 4.5 stay at 200K: on a subscription, Sonnet's 1M variant needs paid usage credits, and Haiku has none.

1.9.0

10 November 2026
  • Codex app context items that arrive as a function_call_output with a name but no call_id (such as codex_apps_open_page) are rewritten once, before any provider, as a user context message <external_NAME>…</external_NAME>. They previously failed every gateway turn on Claude and other translated routes with "Responses request contains invalid or unsupported data". Request telemetry counts them as contextOutputs.

GitHub release ↗Download for Mac

1.8.9

10 November 2026
  • A provider can set cacheMissLimit (3 to 12, default 3) to allow more measured large cache misses in a row before the five-minute cache-safety stop. DeepSeek on OpenRouter builds its prefix cache asynchronously, so a fresh Flash worker could be paused after three cold requests although its cache was still warming. Unknown usage and refusals keep the two-miss limit, and other providers are unchanged.

GitHub release ↗Download for Mac

1.8.8

10 November 2026
  • Chat Completions servers (local Qwen through vLLM) now report every context overflow as context_length_exceeded, including vLLM's "max_tokens must be at least 1, got 0" for a prompt that fills the window exactly and overflow wording without the usual token counts. Codex then compacts instead of ending the turn with an upstream error.
  • A conversation that keeps overflowing a Chat Completions provider stops reaching it after 25 consecutive refusals within ten minutes. The client gets one non-retryable error that asks for a fresh worker with a compact handoff, instead of trimming one history item per request for an hour. Any completed request resets the count.

GitHub release ↗Download for Mac

1.8.7

10 November 2026

  • Large chats get one additional request to recover from two measured cache misses. If reuse still fails, the five-minute cooldown has a fixed deadline that retries cannot extend. After the cooldown, one recovery request can check whether the provider cache is working again. Unknown cache usage and provider refusals retain their earlier spending limits. The error reports the remaining wait and preserves the chat history.

  • Linux rollout checks verify external component executables through procfs, so minimal hosts without lsof can attest a live tunnel while mismatched executables and process start stamps remain pending.

1.8.6

9 November 2026
  • Fixed a rolling-update regression introduced in 1.8.5: changing the gateway auth command spelling and deadline made retained native writers reject new desktop and SSH connections. New clients can attach using the earlier metadata only after proving both command aliases execute identical code for the same managed install. Endpoints, credential arguments, client settings and the existing writer stay exact.

1.8.5

9 November 2026

  • Provider token authentication uses a lightweight CLI path instead of importing the entire provider/service stack. New auth rows permit a bounded 15-second cold start, and new generated command references prefer gatefox. Existing gateway and harness-gateway launchers remain compatible. Fresh installs select GateFox config and install folders and export the canonical gatefox command from all launchers.

  • The sidebar brand is only GateFox. The Harness Gateway subtitle and its spoken accessibility label have been removed.

  • The macOS app includes a Submit an issue link in the sidebar that opens the GateFox feedback board in the default browser.

1.8.4

9 November 2026

  • Home Linux CI now runs successfully with portable platform checks, bounded test memory and deterministic asynchronous test waits. Published release versions and changelog entries are connected to the landing page.

  • Chat-registry caches invalidate when file permissions or ownership change, even when the filesystem reports the same modification and change timestamps.

  • gatefox chats migrate --apply is blocked only by processes on the same Codex home: an engine with another CODEX_HOME (such as Mission Runtime's ~/.codex-primary), a test run, or an inference-only gateway serve no longer stops it. A process without CODEX_HOME counts as ~/.codex.

1.8.2

9 November 2026
  • A cancelled Claude turn whose interrupt times out no longer blocks the chat for an hour. Gateway deliberately closes that CLI and permits a new session on the next caller request, subject to the cache guard. Genuine crashes still keep their replay holds, and the cancelled request is never replayed automatically.

1.8.1

9 November 2026

  • The package is @edihasaj/gatefox. The installer and app builder still accept a backend packaged as @edihasaj/harness-gateway or @edihasaj/subscription-gateway. The Claude Desktop help and errors, the Grok config marker (an old marker is replaced, never duplicated), the native app's type and Swift package, and the README now say GateFox. The README links the 1.8.0 GateFox download.

  • gatefox chats migrate moves saved gateway chats from the provider id subscription_gateway to gatefox. Without --apply it only reports. With --apply it needs ChatGPT and the service stopped, rewrites the provider in each rollout's first line (including the engine's compressed .zst rollouts), copies state_5.sqlite, then moves the chat rows. --revert moves them back. Both ids stay registered.

  • The app's rename to GateFox.app leaves Harness Gateway.app as a link to it. launchd keeps the loaded service's old program path until the next login, and the service plan stores the old app's Node path for the Claude components; without the link, a service restart failed with exit 78 and the Claude adapter could not start until the next login.

1.8.0

9 November 2026

  • A Claude chat whose login fails before any reply, tool result or queued message no longer stays blocked behind a crash hold. The next request tries the saved login again. A failure after the turn produced output keeps the hold, because the turn may have advanced. See docs/claude-sessions.md.

  • A Claude chat whose login fails before any reply, tool result or queued message no longer stays blocked behind a crash hold. The next request tries the saved login again. A failure after the turn produced output keeps the hold, because the turn may have advanced. See docs/claude-sessions.md.

  • The app is GateFox.app, published as GateFox-VERSION-macos-arm64.zip with gatefox-VERSION-macos-arm64.tar.gz, under the standard vVERSION tag only. A Mac updated from 1.7.x first gets the new app at its old Harness Gateway.app path; at its next launch the app renames itself to GateFox.app beside it, relaunches, and moves the service and the command-line runtime to the new path. Permissions stay, because the bundle identifier and signature are unchanged. The rename waits while an update is unfinished. See docs/macos-updates.md.

  • The installer also writes a gatefox command, with the same contents as harness-gateway and gateway, which keep working. An update run by a 1.7.x app adds it at the next install, because that updater refuses receipts it does not know.

  • Fresh installations use ~/.local/share/gatefox and ~/Library/Application Support/GateFox (~/.config/gatefox on Linux). A Mac installed earlier keeps its subscription-gateway folders; nothing moves. The signed service launcher, the updater, uninstall and the app accept both.

  • The Claude Desktop profile and the ChatGPT sign-in agent are named GateFox. A profile created as Harness Gateway is still selected.

  • After a service restart, a desktop, relay session or SSH listener no longer takes the native ChatGPT engine away from the gateway host. The new host's claim could lose to the old host that was still exiting; the next client then started its own private engine, and every later client joined it, so rollout stayed native_owner_pending until every client disconnected. While no private engines hold the native home, a refused client now asks the host again for up to 20 seconds instead.

  • New gateway chats are recorded with the provider id gatefox. Chats saved earlier keep subscription_gateway, which every engine still registers and every list still shows, so nothing needs reopening. gateway desktop register publishes a native row for both ids, so ChatGPT's own engine opens either. The native-config guard refuses both ids. Executors carry GATEFOX_EXECUTOR (and the older marker). The patched SDK is gateway-executor-v4. See docs/harness-identity.md and docs/gatefox-rename.md.

  • gatefox.dev has search and sharing metadata on every page: canonical URLs, Open Graph and Twitter cards with a share image per page, JSON-LD, robots.txt, a sitemap with images and a web manifest. The deploy adds the IndexNow key file.

1.7.6

8 November 2026

  • The app updater now also accepts standard vVERSION release tags and the GateFox release names (GateFox-VERSION-macos-arm64.zip holding GateFox.app, and gatefox-VERSION-macos-arm64.tar.gz). A release must carry app-update.json to count as an app update, so command-line-only releases are ignored. This prepares the 1.8.0 rename; 1.7.6 itself keeps the Harness Gateway names.

  • A public roadmap lists the next steps for contributors: the Claude apps, DeepSeek, and a Chat Completions ingress for other harnesses, each with a GitHub issue.

  • The README and the guide now start with a single-Mac setup: install, connect your accounts, start the service. Adding more Macs is a separate, optional chapter. The long README moved to docs/cli.md, and docs/reference.html is a new searchable index of every doc, generated from each page's summary by npm run docs:site and checked by npm run check.
